raw_response:
*speaking as the farmer*

Well, let me think about this year. I've been doing this 35 years — wheat and maize, wheat and maize, same as my father did. Just me and the old lady now, kids are in the city. Four mu and a bit isn't much but we don't need much.

**My wheat** — I'll plant around early October, right after I clear the maize. Buy a bag of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, and spread it before I till. One 50-jin bag per mu, that's what I've always done. Then in the spring around jointing time I put down urea — maybe 30 jin per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang tried cutting back last year and his wheat looked thin and yellow, so I'm not changing anything.

Water three times — once before the ground freezes to help it through winter, once at jointing in spring, once when the grain is filling. Electricity for the pump costs money but skipping means less grain. If the snow is good maybe I save one watering.

I spray weeds once in spring, cheap stuff from the shop. Usually enough.

Last year I got around 410 kg per mu. I expect about the same — 400, 420 kg maybe.

**My maize** — this is the hard part. When I cut the wheat in June I only got a few days before I need the maize in the ground. I pay my nephew with the no-till planter to come do it. Hybrid seed from the shop, whatever everyone's using this year.

I put compound fertilizer at planting through the planter, then at the big-bell-mouth stage (大喇叭口) I broadcast urea. About 25 jin per mu of urea. 

Maize usually gets enough rain in July-August but if it's dry at tasseling I'll water once. I spray for the corn borer moth if I see damage.

I expect around 450-480 kg per mu. Good years 500.

**Labor** — just me and the wife. At 66 my back hurts but we hire the combine and the planter, pay by the mu. Nothing we can't handle for 4 mu.

**Money** — I don't count it too carefully. Seed, fertilizer, water, pesticide, hired machine — maybe 800 yuan per mu per year, so around 3,500-3,800 yuan total for the year. The kids send us some money; between that and the grain we eat and sell, we get by.
